1 دَبَغَ الإِهَابَ , (S, K,) or الجِلْدَ, (S, Mgh, Msb,) aor.
دَبُغَ and
دَبَغَ (S, Mgh, Msb, K) and دَبْغٌ, (Mgh, Msb, K,) inf. n. دَبْغٌ (S, Mgh, Msb, K) and دِبَاغٌ (S, Mgh, K) and دِبَاغَةٌ, (S, K,) or the last is a subst. sometimes used as an inf. n., (Msb,) He tanned the hide, or skin; i. e., prepared it, or made it fit for use, and softened it, or made it pliable, with قَرَظ [q. v.] and the like. (TA.) It is said in a trad., دِبَاغُهَا طَهُورُهَا [The tanning thereof is the means of purification thereof]. (S, TA.) ―
-b2- See also دَبُوغٌ.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
